*Noted 2026-10-15, from Buffet's `FRONT.1` scoping, relayed by the owner.* Buffet's views move off the Screen. Each, the Portfolio first, will be a sheet of its own shown by its tab, with its Screen holding nothing ("the UI is a workbook"). So this item reaches its client through decision 8, the skip for a sheet shown in the Screen's place, and not through the Screen's path the opening paragraph describes, which was Buffet's state at the minting. Buffet keeps its side under `BD-7`: only the Day sheet reads the frame, so a view is still between market days, and the Day sheet itself never is.

A game's views on its sheets is a new item Buffet asked for, at the next free ID, `ENGINE.18`, not minted here. It covers opening on a named sheet, a click on the shown sheet counted as the game's, the game showing a sheet, the Screen's place in such a cartridge, and key chords. It also covers a shown sheet drawn from the values view after frame 0. Today `refreshSheet` views the grid record, so a still sheet keeps its view's cost every frame; that is the new item's to change, not this one's. It works in the same code, under this item's rule that every load the host makes into a viewport is noted (`_noteLoad`), a load that opens a game on a named sheet included. A load left unnoted is loaded again at the next frame, since the viewport's model is not the one noted: safe, but one load more than the rule allows.

*Owner-tested 2026-10-15 and closed, committed at the owner's word, "Commit".* Buffet ran on Alonzo's page as built from the tree, its text pasted into the drawer, with its Screen tab shown. The drawer's frame line read `Frame 320, the window A1:CB50, drawn by the viewport, 320 of 320 frames still` (a screenshot). Buffet's Screen holds no cell, so its records at frames 0 and 1 are one text and every frame is still, the first among them. Buffet's own page, vendored at `v0.1.3`, has neither the skip nor the count until a release carries them.

## `ENGINE.18` — a grid cartridge's views on its own sheets: the sheet it opens on and the sheet it shows, a click on any sheet the game's, every sheet drawn from the values view, and a Screen it does not use hidden

*Minted and scoped 2026-10-15 at the owner's word, for Buffet, the client; nothing built. Buffet's `FRONT.1` (`Delta/Buffet`: `docs/OMAKASE.md`, and its section of `docs/SPIKE.md`, both uncommitted there on the day) makes the game's interface the workbook itself. Each view, the Portfolio first and then the Market, the Overview, the Exam and Work as their dishes land, is a sheet of its own with its own widths, heights, looks and gridlines, reached by the viewport's own tabs, with no tab strip drawn in cells and no Camera moving between regions of the Screen. The owner's words: "Real sheets are the path forward ("the UI is a workbook"), because Buffet is a mini, blossoming Frazaro, so each Buffet tab should have its own properties as if each were an independent view." `FRONT.1` is gated on this item. The owner's prompt named six needs, each with the dish that needs it first and its spelling this repository's, and restated the second the same hour: `ENGINE.17`'s decision 8 already skips a still sheet's load and paint, and what remains is the view itself. `ENGINE.17`, minted for Buffet the same day, was built and uncommitted in this tree, awaiting the owner; this scoping reads its code as the base, and its note of the day above names this item's rule, every load the host makes into a viewport noted.*

**Substrate, verified.** Read in the code on the day, `c6803d5` with `ENGINE.17`'s hunks, and measured where a decision needed a fact.
- *The opening.* `loadBytes` draws a grid cartridge's Screen at the load, `_drawGrid(true)`, through the Camera's window, and the viewport's sheet is the Screen. A tab clicked is answered (`answer`, `showSheet`, `refreshSheet`), and the Screen's tab gives the Camera's window back (`_screenTab`).
- *A sheet shown.* At every frame a sheet shown in the Screen's place is viewed through `refreshSheet`, which asks `viewRecord` for the `grid` record of the region in view, its formulas' texts with it, at frame 0 and after; the Screen's own frame is the `values` record once `this.frame > 0` (`ENGINE.8`'s second slice). `ENGINE.17` compares each frame's text with the record the host last loaded into that viewport (`_lastLoad`, `_noteLoad`, `_still`) and skips a still one's load and paint; the view runs every frame, its text being what tells.
- *The pointer.* `_windowCellAt` answers null unless the Screen shows, so `Input!B11` to `B15` read 0 over every other sheet (`ENGINE.14`'s decision 4). `_inputRows` writes the window's cell plus the Camera's offset; the buttons follow the pointer; the wheel is the game's over the window's cells alone (decision 5).
- *The layouts.* The engine holds the Input sheet to `A1:E10` and `A11:B18` and the Camera to `A1:B2` (`engine/src/cartridge.rs`, `Device::layout`), makes the Input sheet's eighteen labels when the cartridge holds none (`INPUT_LABELS`, `make_own_sheets`), and prints the extents in `describe`. The double (`web/fake.js`, `LAYOUT`) and `tools/check_cartridge.ps1` (`$layouts`) hold the same layouts of their own.
- *The versions.* The engine reads `(spec 1)` to `(spec 3)` (`SPECS`); the double, `check_cartridge.ps1` for a cartridge and for a replay's header, and the refusal's own words (`engine/data/messages.vla`) say 1 to 3. `(spec 4)` stands for "a later page" in five places: the loop oracle's `refusals` and `parity`, its `replay` case's bad replays, the engine's test `a_later_spec_is_refused_before_its_directives`, and two of `check_cartridge.ps1`'s mutants.
- *The replay's header* names the host's version, `SPEC = 3`. The loop oracle holds each committed replay's re-recording to the replay byte for byte, the header included (`again === rBody`), and the input card's live run to its committed replay; all four committed replays say `(spec 3)`.
- *The player* shows no formula bar: the viewport's `select` event drives `?viewport=1`'s line alone. Its grid box is hidden until the host's `load` event, when the page shows it and redraws the viewport.
- *The keys.* The viewport moves by the arrows, Page Up and Down, Home and End, with Ctrl too, and opens a cell at Enter; it reads no Alt and moves between no sheets by key. The host takes a key the Keys sheet binds before the viewport sees it, and writes the frame's last key as `B17` and `B18`.
- *Measured* over the module as released in 0.1.3, its 749,218 bytes, run in Node 24.21 (*measurement*):
  - Buffet's record lists its sheets in its own order, Screen, Day, Dice, Market and Stocks, then the engine's Clock, File and Input, visible, then every twin hidden.
  - `(sheet "Screen" hidden)` loads and prints hidden; the viewport's strip keeps a hidden sheet behind its box of hidden sheets.
  - A grid cartridge with no Screen sheet loads, and the view of its Screen is refused, `view-sheet-unknown`.
  - `Camera!B3` and `Input!A19` are refused at their lines, `cart-device-cell-outside`, naming `Camera!A1:B2` and `Input!A1:E10 and Input!A11:B18`; `(spec 4)` is refused, `cart-spec-unsupported`.
  - A formula's `value` row carries its value at frame 0: a test formula in `Day!D1` and its value `"Day"` stood in the frame 0 record.

**The measurement before the operation.** The view a still sheet keeps under `ENGINE.17`, by the record it is drawn from. Each sheet viewed through the owner's full screen of default cells, `A1:AN68`, 40 columns by 68 rows (`MISE.3`), after frame 31; the module above in Node 24.21's V8, Chrome's engine; the median of 400 views of each of Buffet's sheets and of 200 of each card, the card run twice; the parse by the viewport's own `readRecord` (*measurement*; runs under three seconds, before Windows' throttle, unpinned).

| the sheet, through `A1:AN68` | the `grid` record: view, bytes, parse | the `values` record: view, bytes, parse |
|---|---|---|
| Buffet's Day | 0.021 ms, 1,066 B, 0.019 ms | 0.013 ms, 867 B, 0.014 ms |
| Buffet's Dice | 0.043 ms, 2,271 B, 0.033 ms | 0.022 ms, 1,567 B, 0.028 ms |
| Buffet's Market | 0.140 ms, 5,923 B, 0.083 ms | 0.048 ms, 3,836 B, 0.069 ms |
| Buffet's Stocks | 0.061 ms, 2,728 B, 0.041 ms | 0.025 ms, 1,828 B, 0.035 ms |
| a card of 1,000 formulas reading the day, `A1:T50`, `FRONT.1`'s cap | 2.0 to 2.2 ms, 86,996 B, 1.15 ms | 0.34 to 0.36 ms, 27,176 B, 0.77 to 0.78 ms |
| the same over the whole region, 2,720 | 5.2 to 5.3 ms, 238,181 B, 3.3 ms | 0.94 to 0.96 ms, 74,389 B, 3.2 to 3.3 ms |

Buffet's sheets today keep a still frame a tenth of a millisecond of view at most, by either record. A view at `FRONT.1`'s cap keeps 2 ms a frame by the grid record and a third of a millisecond by the values record.

**The prediction**, written before the build.
- Every cartridge written to 1 to 3 loads, describes, plays and replays as it did: each committed describe golden, each committed replay's re-recording, the input card's live recording and the floors' digests, byte for byte (*prediction*, exact).
- A still view sheet's frame costs its values view and nothing more. At `FRONT.1`'s cap that is about 1.7 ms less of the main thread a frame in Chrome than by the grid record, near `ENGINE.17`'s still Screen, 0.8 to 1.0 ms a frame, where it would be about 2.5 to 2.9 (*derived*, from the table and `ENGINE.17`'s still frame). Buffet's first light, a Portfolio of a few dozen formulas, saves under a tenth of a millisecond a frame, too little for a frame's timing to show.
- The module grows by under a kilobyte, and the loop oracle's run by one to two seconds a ratio (*prediction*).

**The decisions**, each the scoping's recommendation; the owner's prompt left every spelling to this repository.
1. **The page's version 4, carried by this item, and version 3 kept whole.** Two device layouts gain a row, the Input sheet's nineteenth and the Camera's third. `SPEC.md` §3 refuses a cell outside a layout "so that a later version of this page can add a row without colliding with a cartridge that used it", so a new row is a version's and never a correction's. `(spec 4)` is read, and version 4's rows and behaviors belong to a `(spec 4)` cartridge alone. For a cartridge written to 1, 2 or 3:
   - the engine checks version 3's layouts, makes its Input sheet of eighteen rows, and `describe` prints its extents as before;
   - the host writes it eighteen rows, its pointer 0 off the Screen (`ENGINE.14`'s decision 4), and opens it on its Screen;
   - its replay names version 3 (decision 7).

   The witnesses are the ones every push runs: each committed describe golden, each committed replay's re-recording, the input card's live recording and the floors' digests, byte for byte. The one change every cartridge takes is decision 3, a draw that changes no value, a correction as `ENGINE.8`'s second slice was. *Alternatives:* corrections to version 3 for every cartridge, which the page's own rule forbids; it would move every describe golden and every committed replay's header or rows, and give a version 3 grid cartridge a pointer over sheets it never draws. Or a SPEC ID of its own for the rows, this item the host's: one act in two items with one hand test. *The number:* `SPEC.4`, filed 2026-10-13 as "the page's version 4" for the room's seats, is gated on `REPO.6` and unbuilt; at this item's build its line becomes the page's next version, its ID kept.
2. **The sheet a grid cartridge opens on: the one its Camera names, else its first visible sheet.** (The first need.) At the load of a `(spec 4)` cartridge the host reads the Camera's third row as the load left it, a value or a formula's `value` row, and opens on the sheet it names. When it names none, or the cartridge has no Camera, the host opens on the first visible sheet of the record's `sheet` rows, which follow the cartridge's own order. So Buffet's `(sheets "Portfolio" ...)` opens on the Portfolio with no Camera at all, and a save, its Camera's value row in it, opens where its game stood. The sheet is shown as a tab clicked is (`showSheet`), its load noted under `ENGINE.17`'s rule. *Alternatives:* a manifest directive, `(opens "Portfolio")`, fixed for the grid's life where the Camera's cell may move, a second spelling of what the cell says; the first visible sheet alone, so that a save of a game past its exam opens on the exam again.
3. **Every sheet drawn is the values record after frame 0, for every cartridge.** (The second, as the owner restated it.) Every record the host views to draw a sheet into a viewport is the `values` projection once a frame has computed values, and the `grid` record at frame 0: its own viewport at a frame, and a page's viewer through `showSheet` and `refreshSheet`. That is the Screen's rule since `ENGINE.8`'s second slice, so a formula shows its text until its first value. `viewRecord`, a page's read of a record, stays the grid record. `ENGINE.17`'s comparison holds over the values text as it held over the grid's, so a still sheet's frame keeps only the cheaper view. A person loses a formula's text in the record the viewport holds, which nothing in the player shows; a formula bar, when an item brings one, reads its cell's formula by `viewRecord(sheet, cell)`, the grid record of one cell. *Measured above:* a still sheet at `FRONT.1`'s cap, its view from 2.0 to 2.2 ms to 0.34 to 0.36. *Alternatives:* the grid record at a sheet's showing and values after, the viewport keeping the formula texts it read, since a step never changes a formula (`AD-7`): a merge in the viewport's code, which Frazaro's copy would take too, for a bar nobody has yet. Or values for the host's own viewport alone, two projections of one sheet drawn.
4. **A click on the sheet shown is the game's: the Input sheet's nineteenth row, `sheet`, and the pointer's cell on that sheet.** (The third.) For a `(spec 4)` cartridge at a rate above zero the host writes `Input!B19` with the other rows: the name of the sheet its viewport shows, as the record spells it, a plane's being the Screen. `B11` and `B12` become the pointer's column and row on that sheet: through the Camera's window on the Screen, as before; on any other sheet, the sheet's own cell under the pointer, any cell in view; 0 over the headers, the corner, the tabs and the scrollbars (`cellAt`). The buttons follow the pointer, so a press on a tab is never the game's, and the context menu is the game's over a cell that is. A button is then `B19`, `B11`, `B12` and the rising edge of `B13`, kept once in a cell that holds 0 between presses (`FRONT.1`'s own rule; §2's rule 3). The replay logs `B19` as it logs every Input cell that changes, so a person's tab is a row of the replay, and a game that reads it replays. The wheel stays the game's over the Screen's window alone (`ENGINE.14`'s decision 5); over another sheet it scrolls, a sheet being read by scrolling. *Why the sheet shown and not the sheet under the pointer:* off the cells `B11` and `B12` say 0 either way, and the name is then always the person's tab, a fact a game may read on its own; none asks yet. *Alternatives:* the sheet under the pointer, empty off the cells; `B11` and `B12` kept the Screen's, and three rows more for a sheet's pointer; the sheet's index in the tab order, which the cartridge's own reordering would move.
5. **The game shows a sheet: the Camera's third row, `sheet`.** (The fourth.) The Camera becomes three cells, `row`, `column` and `sheet`, read at the load (decision 2) and after each step with the other two. When `B3`'s value changes from the frame before and names a sheet the grid holds, compared without case as the model compares names, the host shows it at the frame's end as a tab clicked is shown: the Screen through the Camera's window as its tab gives it back, any other sheet through `showSheet`. Between its changes the person's tabs win, as the person's scroll wins between the Camera's moves (§3.8). Empty, or a formula before its first value, names no sheet and moves nothing. A name the grid does not hold, a number, an error or a truth value is said once, as a Camera cell is (`SD-30`), and moves nothing. The row and the column stay the Screen's window's place and never scroll another sheet. In plane mode the plane draws the Screen, and a sheet the Camera names is said once. `GUARD.1`'s exam ending on the Portfolio is then `=IF(Exam!B1=1,"Portfolio","Exam")`, its change shown once. *Alternatives:* a device sheet of its own, a new reserved name for one cell. The row and the column scrolling the sheet the Camera names, which makes two cells mean two things by the sheet, and leaves a cartridge with a world on its Screen and a ledger on a sheet unable to hold its Screen's window. The cell as a level, its sheet shown at every frame, which takes the tabs from the person.
6. **A Screen the views do not use is hidden, by the row version 3 already reads.** (The fifth.) With `(sheet "Screen" hidden)` the strip keeps the Screen's tab behind its box of hidden sheets, a `(spec 4)` cartridge never opens on it (decision 2), and the host never views it until it is shown, by the Camera or by a person who ticks the box. The manifest's `(screen grid 80 50)` keeps its words: the mode, and the window a Screen is drawn through when it is shown, so an ending or a crash screen (Buffet's `FRONT.7`) can be the Screen a game shows. A grid cartridge with no Screen loads too (measured) and works under decisions 2 and 5: nothing views its Screen, and a Camera that names one is said once. *Recommended for Buffet:* hidden, so that its manifest's screen line stays true and its Screen stays where `AD-6` can see it. *Alternatives:* none; a manifest spelling for a cartridge without a Screen, `(screen grid)`, a directive for no frame.
7. **A replay's header names the page its rows are written to: its cartridge's version, and 3 for a cartridge written to 1 to 3.** The host implements version 4 and reads replays of 1 to 4. The header has named the host's version, and the loop oracle holds each committed replay's re-recording to the replay byte for byte, header included, and the input card's live run to its committed replay. A header of 4 on a version 3 cartridge's replay would fail both and leave no committed replay standing. A version 3 cartridge's replay holds version 3's rows (decision 1) and says so; a `(spec 4)` cartridge's says 4, and an older host refuses it by name, which is the header's purpose. *Alternative:* the host's version always, and the four committed replays rewritten.
8. **The limits: a sheet shown is drawn through the region in view, and the 80 by 50 stays the Screen's.** A view sheet declares no window: it is drawn through the cells its viewport shows (`ENGINE.14`'s decision 3), 2,720 default cells at the owner's full screen and more on a larger screen. Measured above, a whole such region of formulas views in about 1 ms from values and parses in about 3.3. §10 says so, and a cartridge keeps its own budget, Buffet's 1,000 formula cells in view (`MISE.3`). *Alternative:* the region held to 80 by 50 cells, blank past it on a large screen.
9. **Key chords: a sitting recorded here, built as an item of its own after this one.** (The sixth.) Its three questions, each with the first pass's recommendation. The exhibits are dated 2026-10-15, and a probe settles them before any build.
   - *What the browser keeps.* In a window Chrome never hands a page new tab (Ctrl+T), new window (Ctrl+N), a new incognito window, close tab (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+F4), close window, restore tab (Ctrl+Shift+T), next tab (Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+PageDown), previous tab (Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Ctrl+PageUp) or exit. In fullscreen it keeps exit and the fullscreen toggle alone, every other command delivered to the page (Chromium's `IsReservedCommandOrKey`, its list as a revision of the source reads it, *exhibit*). So Excel's Ctrl+PageDown and Ctrl+PageUp, the next and previous sheet, are the browser's in a window and the page's in fullscreen, where Buffet is played. Windows keeps Alt+Tab, Alt+F4, Alt+Space and Alt+Esc. Alt with a letter or an arrow is none of Chrome's reserved commands, so a page has it first and may cancel it, as Google's editors take Alt+F; left to the browser, each is a command (Alt+Left back, Alt+Right forward, Alt+F and Alt+E the menu, Alt+D the address bar). Firefox keeps Alt for its menu bar, so Google's editors take Alt+Shift with a letter there (Google's help, *exhibit*). On macOS Option with a letter types a character, so a chord is matched by `code` and never `key`. The Keyboard Lock API takes reserved keys only in a fullscreen the page itself asked for, in Chrome and Edge alone (Chrome's documentation, *exhibit*). *Recommended:* the chord as Excel's key tips make it, Alt pressed and released alone and then a sequence of single keys, never Alt held with a letter, so that no step of a chord is a browser's accelerator. The host cancels every key a sequence takes, Escape steps back, and a key no chord continues ends the sequence, said. First, a probe page the owner runs in Chrome, Edge and Firefox, measuring what a cancel stops, Alt's own release among it.
   - *What the workbook keeps.* Moving between sheets first: Ctrl+PageDown and Ctrl+PageUp, Excel's, wherever the browser hands them over; and the sequence Alt then a sheet's key tip, the strip lettering each visible tab while the sequence waits, as Excel letters its ribbon's tabs. A sheet's letter is its name's first free one and never a number, since tabs are not serial (`BD-2`'s amendment). The cartridge's chords take the letters the sheets leave, or sit under a prefix of their own: the sitting's question for the owner.
   - *How a cartridge declares its own.* A device sheet, `Chords`, a row a chord: column A its keys after Alt as codes (`KeyB KeyS`), column B the words its key tip shows. A chord completed is written into the Input sheet as its row's number for one frame, `B20`, as `key` is written. So a chord is an input like a press, logged and replayed, and a person rebinds one by editing its row: the Keys sheet's "Emacs's keymap as a cell edit" (§3.4) grown into Emacs's own prefix keymaps. A row of the Input sheet and a device sheet make it the page's version 5 when it lands.

   *Filed* as its own item at the owner's word, the next free ID, after this item's release; Buffet's `MISE.6` asks for it before the first dish that needs a chord. *Alternatives:* chords in this item, holding `FRONT.1` for a sitting it does not need; a chord pressing one of the ten buttons, ten names for every command a workbook has.
10. **The oracle.** The loop oracle's twenty-second case, `views`, over the module. Its card is inline, as the still card is, and never a file, so that by `ENGINE.16`'s rule it runs on a game's page too, holding the vendored host there. The card, `(spec 4)` at rate 30:
    - the Screen listed first and hidden;
    - a Desk sheet, with a button at `C5` and a press count, `=Desk.last!B2+IF(AND(Input!B19="Desk",Input!B11=3,Input!B12=5,Input!B13=1,Input.last!B13=0),1,0)`;
    - a Ledger of a few hundred formulas reading only the day, the still card's spelling, and a Day;
    - a Camera whose `B3` is a formula of the frame, empty until frame 40, `"Ledger"` from 40 and `"Screen"` from 70.

    Over 90 frames:
    - frame 0 opens on Desk, the first visible sheet, the hidden Screen never viewed until frame 70. A second run, its `B3` given a `value` row of `"Ledger"`, opens on Ledger, and the formula's first value at frame 1, empty, moves nothing;
    - every frame from 1 draws the sheet shown from the values record, held cell for cell to the record as the `grid` case holds a window, `ENGINE.17`'s choice of a still frame held to the oracle's own;
    - a press over `Desk!C5` from frame 10 to 12 writes `B19` "Desk", `B11` 3, `B12` 5 and `B13` 1, and the count reads 1; a press over Desk's column header and over the tabs writes 0 and 0 and counts nothing;
    - the person's tab to Ledger at frame 20 puts "Ledger" in frame 21's `B19`, and a press over `Ledger!C5` counts nothing on the Desk;
    - the person's tab back to Desk at frame 30; the Camera's "Ledger" shown at frame 40; the person's Desk at frame 50, kept through frame 69 while the Camera says "Ledger"; the Camera's "Screen" at frame 70, drawn through its window; the person's Desk at frame 80;
    - the run's replay, its header `(spec 4)` and its `B19` rows, played on a fresh host to the same count and Input record at every frame;
    - version 3 kept: the grid card, `(spec 3)`, its Camera's tab clicked and the pointer over a cell there, writes `B11` and `B12` 0 and no row 19, and opens on its Screen.

    Mutant pages, lettered after `ENGINE.17`'s, each failing `views` by name and proving it applied: a host that opens a `(spec 4)` cartridge on its Screen; one that opens on its first sheet, hidden or not; one that draws a sheet shown from the grid record after frame 0; one whose pointer is 0 off the Screen; one that writes no `B19`; one that writes the pointer off the Screen for a `(spec 3)` cartridge too; one that reads the Camera's sheet at the load alone; one that shows it at every frame; and one whose replay of a version 3 cartridge names version 4, failing the `replay` and `input` cases. The engine's tests: a `(spec 4)` cartridge loads; `Camera!B3` and `Input!A19` within version 4's layouts, and refused under `(spec 3)` naming version 3's; the Input sheet the engine makes holds nineteen labels at version 4 and eighteen before; `describe`'s extents by version; a `(spec 5)` refused; every committed describe golden unchanged. `check_cartridge.ps1` reads `(spec 4)` for a cartridge and for a replay's header, with mutants for version 4's rows under `(spec 3)`.
11. **One slice and one commit, built on `ENGINE.17`'s commit.** Version 4 is one page, its engine half and its host half landing and tested together, and no part of it is worth a release alone. It changes the four places `ENGINE.17` built in (the frame's draw of a sheet, `showSheet`, `refreshSheet` and the load), so it starts from `ENGINE.17`'s commit and keeps its rule, every load the host makes into a viewport noted, the opening and the Camera's show among them. The engine changes, so a release follows at the owner's word, its version the owner's to name; then Buffet pins and vendors its tag and rescopes `FRONT.1`, in the owner's order.
12. **The record.** `SPEC.md` rewritten in place as version 4, as versions 2 and 3 were: §3.1 (the views, the opening, the hidden Screen, every sheet from values), §3.3 (the nineteenth row and the pointer on the sheet shown), §3.8 (the Camera's third row), §4.2 (`(spec 4)` and the layouts by version), §5's steps 3, 5 and 6, §7.2, §7.6 (the header), §8.3, §10 (a sheet's region), §11's decisions from 36, §12 and §13. `ROADMAP.md`'s `SPEC.4` line becomes the next version's. `web/README.md`, `docs/RELEASES.md` at the release, the map in `Delta/CLAUDE.md`, and the memory. The charter needs no amendment: `AD-6` gains two cells, the sheet a person shows and the sheet a game shows.

**Not this item, named.**
- Key chords, decision 9's item.
- The wheel over a view sheet, which `ENGINE.14`'s decision 5 declined to give a game without knowing what it reads.
- A game scrolling a sheet or moving its selection, the Camera's row and column for the sheet it names, when a view wants one.
- A save opening on the sheet a person last saw, `Input!B19` in the save, the save's shape being `ENGINE.5`'s.
- A replay showing the recorded person's tabs as it plays.
- The formula bar.
- The owner's horizon, a cartridge loaded as a tab beside a spreadsheet's sheets, "so Kairos could be a tab beside any other sheet". It is not built and not designed against: the sheet shown is a name in two cells, and nothing here says how a sheet is drawn, so a later page may draw a named sheet by another projection.

**The catch.**
- The opening sheet's region is read off a viewport the player shows only at the host's `load` event. Viewed from `A1` over a box of no size, it is a region of one cell (`ENGINE.14`'s catch), and at rate zero no frame would view it again: the host views it again once the viewport is laid out.
- Every load the host makes into a viewport is noted (`ENGINE.17`'s rule), the opening and the Camera's show included; a load left unnoted is loaded again at the next frame.
- The Camera's show at a frame's end and the frame's own draw must not view the sheet twice, nor count a sheet just shown as still.
- On the Screen the pointer is the window's cell and the Camera is added; on another sheet it is the sheet's own cell and nothing is added. The host holds which.
- `isScreen('')` is true, nothing shown yet being the Screen: the host keeps the sheet it shows itself, with or without a viewport element, so that a hidden Screen is never viewed by a host that has none.
- `(spec 4)` names "a later page" in five places (the substrate's list), each moved to `(spec 5)` by content.

## `ENGINE.19` — a frame read by its changes: a window patched from the cells the last frame changed, the devices read the same way, and the Input rows written only when one changed

*Minted and scoped 2026-10-15 at the owner's word, Alonzo's half of Frazaro's `KERNEL.42`; nothing built but the pin. `ENGINE.17`'s decision 10 filed the ask, the language's report of a window's changes, so that a host skips the view of a still window too. Frazaro built it as `KERNEL.42` (`fb64e3a`) and released it in `vla-lang` 0.9.4 (`e8911f6`): a fourth projection by name, `changes`, and no new export. The owner's prompt moved the pin first and named Alonzo's half in five parts, each taken by a decision below. "Measure in Chrome before and after, on the still card and on Buffet." Frazaro's tree was read nowhere; the language was read in the registry's copy of 0.9.4.*

- (a) The host asks for a window's changes before viewing it. If `<since>` is the frame of the record it holds, for the same window, it patches the held record and the viewport's model instead of viewing; if `<at>` is that frame, the frame is still; otherwise it views as today (decisions 2 and 3).
- (b) The viewport repaints only the named cells, the DOM diff's step (`ENGINE.20`; decision 1).
- (c) The device reads, a grid view of the Clock, the File and the Camera at every frame, go through changes (decision 4).
- (d) The Input rows are written only when one of them changed: natively the largest part of what a still frame has left, about 60 of 83 µs (decision 5).
- (e) The double: its refusal's words, and a `changes` answer (decision 6).

*The pin at `vla-lang` 0.9.4, 2026-10-15, at the owner's word, the prompt's first step.*

The release is Frazaro's `e8911f6`, carrying `KERNEL.42` (`fb64e3a`).
- A fourth projection, `changes`, written into `SPEC.md` §4.5 as a dated correction of the day. Its answer is a header, `(changes "<sheet>" "<range>" <since> <at> <n>)`, then each changed cell's rows exactly as `values` prints them, in row-major order, with `(empty "<sheet>" "<addr>")` for a cell with none; or the header ending `whole`. The host's rule: holding the window's `values` record at frame `<since>`, replace each named cell's rows with the given ones, and the result is the record at `<at>`, byte for byte.
- Natively, by Frazaro's measurement, relayed: a still window answers in 0.6 to 0.8 µs against `values`' 4 to 178 µs, and about 0.5 µs a changed cell.
- `view-projection-unknown`'s words name the four; its id is unchanged. No signature changed, and no git rev was pinned between 0.9.3 and it.

**Substrate, verified.** Read in the code on the day, `199789c` (`ENGINE.18`'s commit) with the pin's hunks; measured where a decision needed a fact.
- *The frame path* (`web/host.js`).
  - A frame begins with the derived writes, then `_issueInputs`: at a rate above zero, the Input sheet's eighteen rows (nineteen at version 4) as one write at every frame, recorded by `_recordInputs`, then each person's edit as its own write.
  - Its end, `_complete`, reads the Camera and the Palette, draws, then reads the Keys, the Audio, the File, the Write sheet and the Clock. Each read is a `grid` view of the whole sheet, parsed into its cells (`_cells`, `sheetCells`); the Palette compares its record's text with the last.
  - The Screen's draw (`_drawGrid`) views `values` through the Camera's window; a sheet in the Screen's place is viewed through the region in view (`refreshSheet`). `ENGINE.17`'s comparison then skips the load and the paint of a record byte for byte the last one loaded while the viewport still holds the model it made of it (`_lastLoad`, `_noteLoad`, `_still`).
  - The player's drawer refreshes its viewer at a frame's event at most every 200 ms, and at every frame at rate zero (`refreshViewer`).
- *The recorder* logs the Input cells that changed against its own record of the sheet. That record is forgotten, and the next frame's rows logged whole, after a person's edit of the Input sheet and after a replay's rows (`_recordEdit`, `_recordPlayed`). A replay plays back only the cells it logged, so a replay already writes only the Input rows that changed, and every committed replay plays to its golden.
- *The engine's Input sheet.* A formula into a cell the host writes is refused at the load and at a write (`cart-device-cell-formula`), and a derived write into the Input sheet is refused (`cart-write-derived`). So only the host's rows, a person's edit and a replay's rows write the Input sheet, each through the host.
- *The language's changes*, read in 0.9.4's `src/machine/mod.rs`.
  - `at` is the machine's frame and `since` is `at - 1`, so the answer is the last complete frame's alone.
  - Its cells are the twin cells that frame's end changed, inside the window, less those a record spells as before (`ALIKE`, 64 kept).
  - It is whole after a frame that computes every cell next (`every_next`: more changes than its room, `cells / 2 + 64`, or a twin that gained or lost a cell), after more alike changes than it keeps, or after a write before the frame that changed a formula or added a cell (`reshaped`). Between frames it is whole while `reshaped`, or while a value written since lies in the window.
- *Measured* over the module of the pin in Node 24.21 (*measurement*):
  - Before any step the answer is `(changes "S" "R" 0 0 whole)`, and after frame 1 `0 1 whole`; after frame f, `f-1 f` and the cells. An empty window is the sheet's extent, as it is for `values` (the Clock's is `A1:B3`).
  - The still card's day boundary answers whole: 401 of its Screen's formulas change at once, past the room.
  - A value written into the window answers whole until the next frame's end, which names it, and the frame after that answers 0.
  - A formula whose value turns to a reason (`not-computed`) or to an error answers whole, its twin gaining or losing a cell.
  - A reference to an empty cell reads 0, so no `(empty ...)` row arose on any card.
  - An unknown projection's words name the four.
  - *The rule, held.* A probe kept each watched window's last values record and its frame. After every frame it patched the record when `since` was that frame, kept it when `at` was, and viewed whole otherwise, then held the result to the `values` view of the same window byte for byte. No record differed:

    | card | frames | windows watched | patched (cells) | still | whole |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | the still card, its plan's edits and the Camera's move | 90 | the Screen, Board, Day, Clock, File, Camera | 176 (577) | 258 | 21 |
    | Buffet | 200 | Stocks, Market, Day, Dice, the Screen, Clock, File | 416 (696) | 977 | 14 |
    | a probe card: cells changing on rules of the frame, a long text, a value an edit rewrites, a formula written | 40 | the Screen, the Day through two windows, Clock | 148 (289) | 0 | 16 |

  - *The Input rows.* Two grids of one cartridge were driven by one scripted person. The first was written the eighteen rows whole at every frame. The second was written only the rows that changed since the rows it last wrote, whole at the first frame and after a person's edit of the Input sheet. Every sheet's grid record was equal at every frame over the input card's 240 frames, the still card's 120 and Buffet's 120, with 0 differences; the second grid was written at 37, 18 and 18 of them.
  - *The costs*, each the median of 200 calls, in microseconds in V8. The still card is `ENGINE.17`'s, through `A1:CB50`; Buffet's Stocks is through the owner's full screen of default cells, `A1:AN68`, after frame 31.

    | a still frame's call | the still card | Buffet's Stocks |
    |---|---|---|
    | the Input sheet's 48 rows written | 51.5 | 51.7 |
    | the step | 5.4 | 6.3 |
    | the Clock's `grid` view | 9.8 | 11.3 |
    | the File's `grid` view | 8.5 | 10.2 |
    | the Camera's `grid` view | 7.7 | none |
    | the window's `values` view | 143.0 | 27.5 |
    | the sum | 225.9 | 107.0 |
    | the window's `changes` | 2.8 | 4.7 |
    | a device's `changes` | 2.6 | 2.9 to 3.6 |

    Two of the 48 rows write in 4.1 µs. A step after a write of rows that changed nothing costs more on a cartridge that reads them, since a written cell's readers are computed again: 42 µs on the input card against 10.7 after no write. The still card and Buffet step in 3.6 and 4.5 µs after no write, about as after one.

**The measurement before the operation.** The instrument is `ENGINE.17`'s scratch page script, given a sheet to show in the Screen's place, over the page built at the pin, `ENGINE.18`'s host over 0.9.4. It runs in headless Chrome 155 on the GPU at the owner's full screen, 2,560 by 1,440 CSS pixels at a ratio of 1.5 (a canvas of 3,840 by 2,117), its processes opted out of power throttling and pinned to the performance cores. Each run times `runFrameSync`'s frames 21 to 140 after 20 warm, and is held when its clock moved 10% or less (*measurement*):

| frames 21 to 140, 116 of them still | frame p50 | p95 | max | a still frame: main, sync | a drawn frame: main, sync | main thread a frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the still card's Screen (3 runs of 4 held) | 0.5 to 0.6 ms | 0.8 to 1.1 | 3.3 to 4.8 | 0.5 to 0.6, 0.4 to 0.5 | 3.0 to 3.3, 2.5 to 2.8 | 0.80 to 0.90 |
| Buffet's Stocks in the Screen's place (6 runs of 10 held) | 0.4 | 0.7 to 0.8 | 1.4 to 3.7 | 0.4, 0.3 | 1.3 to 1.5, 1.1 to 1.3 | 0.57 to 0.62 |

**The prediction**, written before the build.
- In V8 the module's calls on a still frame fall from 226 µs to about 14 on the still card, and from 107 to about 16 on Buffet's Stocks: the step after no write, one `changes` a device, and the window's `changes` (*derived*, from the table).
- In Chrome a still frame's sync falls from 0.4 to 0.5 ms, and from 0.3, to 0.0 to 0.1, the timer's grain; its frame p50 falls to 0.1 to 0.2. The main thread a frame falls from 0.80 to 0.90 ms to 0.40 to 0.55 on the still card, and from 0.57 to 0.62 to 0.30 to 0.40 on Buffet (*derived*: what a still frame keeps is Chrome's own frame, about 0.3 to 0.4 ms by `ENGINE.17`'s runs, and the host's own work).
- The still card's boundaries stay whole frames, drawn as before at 3.0 to 3.3 ms. Buffet's market days are patched: they lose their view and their parse, about 0.1 ms of 1.3 to 1.5, and their paint stays whole until `ENGINE.20`.
- Exactly: every committed replay, re-recording, describe golden and digest unchanged, and every case's counts as before but the new counters (*prediction*, exact).

**The decisions**, each the scoping's recommendation.
1. **Two items: this one the host's and the double's, (a), (c), (d) and (e), and `ENGINE.20` the viewport's repaint, (b).** The four parts are one frame path and one hand test, each a change in what the host asks of the module. The repaint is the viewport's own and has an oracle of its own, the canvas's pixels; `ENGINE.17`'s decision 10 named it that half, unminted. It depends on this item's patch, and its measured share differs: a still frame paints nothing under either item, and a market day's paint is about 1 ms once in 30 frames. *Alternatives:* one ID in two slices; or five IDs, one a part, though (e) is (a)'s double and (c) is (a)'s path again.
2. **A window's changes before its view, at a frame's own draw.** (a) This covers the Screen's draw through the Camera's window, and `refreshSheet`'s `still` refresh: the frame's draw of a sheet in the Screen's place, and a page's refresh that passes it, the drawer's among them. For each viewport the host keeps, beside `ENGINE.17`'s last load, that load's frame, sheet, window as asked and projection. When the viewport still holds that model, the sheet and the window are the same and the projection is `values`, the host asks for the window's changes:
   - `whole`: it views as today, and `ENGINE.17`'s comparison of the text still finds a still record;
   - `<at>` the held frame: the frame is still, nothing having stepped since the record;
   - `<since>` the held frame and `<n>` 0: still;
   - `<since>` the held frame and `<n>` above 0: the held text and the viewport's model are patched (decision 3);
   - otherwise it views as today.

   A load, `showSheet`, the Screen's tab, a scroll's refresh and `redraw()` always view whole; `redraw()` is the explicit "draw again", whose time the blit's baseline measures. On the frame path the held record is always the last frame's, so `<since>` guards a page's refresh, which may come frames apart: the drawer's views whole as today at a rate above zero, and patches at rate zero, where a frame is an edit. A host with no viewport patches its text alone. *Alternative:* the changes asked of the Screen alone, which leaves Buffet, whose views are sheets in the Screen's place, as it is.

   (*Corrected 2026-10-15*, the build: the window is compared in the answer's header, which names the window asked as the language spells it, and not before the ask. One comparison then serves the Screen, a sheet in its place and the device sheets, whose window is the sheet's extent, and mutant `BN` cuts that one line; a moved window costs one `changes` call, about 3 µs, before its whole view. The host notes the viewport's count of patches with each load as well as its model. And a frame the changes find still hands the held record to `ENGINE.17`'s test of a record viewed whole, `_still`, so that one test decides every still frame, decision 9's correction.)
3. **The patch: the held text byte for byte, and the viewport's model with it, in place.**
   - The host keeps the held record's rows by cell, made at its first patch. A named cell's rows are replaced with the given ones, an `empty` row's cell is removed, and a cell the record lacks goes in at its place in row-major order.
   - The text is joined at once, so that `this.record`, the last load's text and `ENGINE.17`'s comparison stay strings, as today; the join costs a patched frame alone.
   - The viewport gains `patch(text)`. It reads the rows as `readRecord` reads them, one reading of a row serving both, and replaces each named cell's entry in the model it holds, the model's counts with it. It counts its patches, and the host notes that count with the load, so that a model a page patched is never taken for the host's (`ENGINE.17`'s guard, extended). In this item it repaints whole; `ENGINE.20` makes the repaint the cells'.

   *Why the text as well:* `host.record` and `_lastLoad(vp).text` are what the loop oracle holds byte for byte to the `values` view (the `grid`, `still` and `views` cases), so the rule's proof is pins the oracle already has. *Alternatives:* the model alone, the text made when a reader asks; or the text alone, the model loaded again from it, though the parse is what a patch saves (0.77 ms for a 27 KB record, `ENGINE.18`'s table).
4. **Every device read by its changes, all seven.** (c) The owner named the Clock, the File and the Camera, the three the still card reads at every frame. The same path serves the Palette, the Keys, the Audio and the Write sheet, so one rule reads them all. The host keeps each device sheet's cells as last read, with their frame, and asks for the sheet's changes over its extent, an empty window:
   - `whole`, at frame 0 and the frame after a load: the sheet is read whole, as today;
   - `<at>` the held frame, or `<n>` 0: the cells are kept;
   - `<since>` the held frame: the named cells are replaced, and an `empty` row's address is removed.

   Each device's own reading of its cells runs as today, over the kept cells. So the Write sheet's rows still become every frame's derived writes, every edge is found as it was, and the Palette makes its table again only when its cells changed. *Alternative:* the three alone, the other four left to a later measurement.
5. **The Input rows: only those that changed are written.** (d) The host keeps the rows it last wrote. At each frame at a rate above zero it writes the rows that differ from them, in their order, and nothing when none does. It writes them whole at the first frame, after a person's edit of the Input sheet lands (the sheet named without case, as the recorder names it), after a replay's rows and after a refused write; a load forgets them too. The recorder is given the frame's rows whenever they differ from the last written, and is otherwise not called, where it would have logged nothing. Its record of the sheet and the host's are forgotten at the same acts, so every replay keeps its bytes of today. The wheel's notches and the last key are cleared at every frame, as now. *Measured above:* 0 differences over 480 frames of three cards, and the write of two rows in 4.1 µs against 47; and a replay already plays back only the cells that changed. *Alternative:* the rows whole whenever one changed, the prompt's words read narrowly: the same gain on a still frame, and 47 µs at a frame where the pointer moved and two rows changed.
6. **The double answers `changes`.** (e) `view-projection-unknown`'s words name the four. The double keeps the `values` rows of every cell at the last two frames' ends, and answers the cells in the window whose rows differ, in row-major order, `(empty ...)` for a cell with none. It answers whole:
   - before the first frame since the load;
   - after a write that changed a formula or added a cell, until and at the next frame's end;
   - while a value written since the last frame lies in the window;
   - when the window's sheet changed its extent between the two frames, since the record's header would change; its Write sheet's rows do so on a rule of the frame.

   It keeps room for every change, as its `RULES` say, so its Screen, whose tiles all change at every frame, is patched whole at every frame: the patch held at up to four thousand cells a frame, which the module's room never asks for.
7. **What a page sees.**
   - Two counters: `patches`, the frames drawn from their changes, each also a draw; and `inputsKept`, the frames whose Input rows all stood as last written.
   - The timing: a patched frame's is `{ view, draw, patched }`, `patched` being its cells and `view` the changes' time. A still frame's keeps `ENGINE.17`'s shape, its view the changes' time.
   - The drawer's frame line in grid mode: `S of N frames still and P patched`.

   The held records and the last rows written are the host's own state, invisible to formulas; `SPEC.md` §8.3's list of that state grows by both.
8. **The oracle**, in three parts.
   - *The loop oracle's twenty-third case, `changes`*, over the module. Its card is inline, as the still card is, so by `ENGINE.16`'s rule it runs on a game's page too. The card is at rate 30, a grid of 20 by 10. Its Screen holds a cell of the frame, a cell of every seventh frame, a long text on even frames, a value an edit rewrites, and a fill of 64 formulas reading only the day, so that a boundary changes 64 cells, under the room. The card also has a Day, a Camera, a Keys sheet, a Write row landing a value in the Day at every frame, and a File whose save cell rises every 25th frame. Over 60 frames, at every frame:
     - the host's choice for the Screen, whole, patched or still, is the oracle's own from its own `changes` after the frame, and the counters move by it;
     - `host.record` is the `values` view byte for byte;
     - the viewport's model is cell for cell, its counts included, the one a load of that record makes;
     - the drawn window is held to the record;
     - the module's calls, counted by projection through a wrapper: no `values` or `grid` view on a still or patched frame, a `changes` for each device, and a device's `grid` view only where its changes said whole;
     - the host's device state equals a whole read's: the window, the key map, the derived writes, the rate and the save edges;

     - the Camera's move at 40 is whole, the window being new, and the patches start again at 41;

     - the run's replay, played on a fresh host, reaches every frame's Input record and Screen.
   - *The pins moved.* `ENGINE.17`'s `still` and `stillSheets` read a load by the model's identity, which a patch keeps (the catch); they read a patch by the host's counters and the viewport's count, every choice of theirs standing. `views`, `grid` and `still` keep holding the text the host drew to the `values` view, now through patches too. The oracle's own model of the loop writes the rows that changed at step 3. Over the double, the `grid` case is patched at every frame from the second.

**The catch.**
- A patch keeps the viewport's model object, and `ENGINE.17`'s pins read a load by that object's identity. They must read a patch by the host's counters and the viewport's count, or every patched frame of the Day and the Board fails them.
- On the frame path the held record is always the last frame's, so a host that drops the `<since>` comparison fails no case that refreshes at every frame: `BL` needs the oracle's second viewer, refreshed every third frame.
- The recorder is given the rows exactly when they differ from the last written. Its record and the host's must be forgotten at the same acts, or a replay changes by a row.
- A device's reading reads its kept cells and never changes them, and the Write sheet's rows become derived writes at every frame from the kept cells, as they did from a fresh read.
- A formula whose value turns to a reason or an error makes its frame whole (measured), so the case's card keeps its formulas' values plain.
- The double's Write sheet changes its extent on a rule of the frame, so its `whole` there comes from the extent's rule, not a write's.
- PowerShell 5.1 as every check met it: ASCII, `return ,$list`. A script with a backslash goes through the Write tool: on the day, the Bash tool's heredoc collapsed two backslashes into one.
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` and this file are CRLF.

## `ENGINE.20` — a patch repainted cell by cell: the viewport repaints only the cells a window's changes name, the rest of its canvas kept

*Minted and scoped 2026-10-15 at the owner's word, with `ENGINE.19`, whose decision 1 gives the reason for two items. It is the prompt's (b): "The viewport repaints only the named cells (the DOM-diff step)." `ENGINE.17`'s decision 10 left this half to the viewport, unminted, in the owner's reading of `KERNEL.42` as the precursor of a diff of the drawn grid against its last draw, as a DOM diff is. It builds on `ENGINE.19`'s `patch`; nothing is built.*

**Substrate, verified.** `web/viewport.js` at `199789c`.
- *The paint.* `_draw` paints the canvas whole, in this order:
  - a clear, then the background;
  - the body, then up to three frozen quadrants, each clipped to its rectangle. Each paints its fills (a look's, a styled cell's, or a styled column's for its empty cells), then its gridlines a device pixel wide, then its texts, then the selection and the marks;
  - the frozen separators;
  - the headers.

  Every op is recorded (`this.ops`), and `draws()` hands them to the loop oracle, whose held windows (`gqCompare`) compare them with the record cell for cell.
- *What a cell's paint depends on:*
  - its entry: the text, the kind, the value's kind, the style and the look;
  - its column's width, since a number too wide draws #s;
  - whether the cells to its right are empty, since a left-aligned text that does not wrap spills into them;
  - a text up to eight columns to its left (`OVERFLOW_LOOKBACK`) that spills into it;
  - the selection and the marks, painted over it.
- *No value moves the geometry.* Widths come from the record's column rows and heights from its row rows, with no fit to the content, and the frozen panes, the window and the extent stand. A change in any of them makes the answer whole, so it never reaches a patch (`ENGINE.19`).
- *The canvas is current after every event.* A scroll draws at its event and a resize at the observer's; a ratio's change, a selection, a freeze, a width and a mark draw at once. The one state in which the canvas lags is a scroll whose event has not yet fired: the scroller is then not at `lastScroll`.
- *The calls.* A text is drawn by `fillText`, clipped to its cell's span (`Painter.text`); fills and gridlines sit at whole device pixels.

**The measurement before the operation.** Buffet's Stocks in the Screen's place at the owner's full screen, `ENGINE.19`'s table. Its four drawn frames of 120, the market days, take a main-thread p50 of 1.3 to 1.5 ms, 1.1 to 1.3 of it the frame's own work. Its `values` view is 0.025 ms and its parse 0.035 (`ENGINE.18`'s table), so nearly all of a drawn frame is the paint, which `ENGINE.19`'s patch leaves whole. The still card's boundaries are whole frames, 401 cells past the room, and full paints under either item.

**The prediction**, written before the build.
- A patched frame of a few cells repaints in 0.05 to 0.1 ms, where a full paint at full screen is about 1 ms.
- Buffet's market day falls from 1.3 to 1.5 ms of main thread to 0.2 to 0.4: about 0.03 ms a frame over a market day's 30 frames (*derived*).
- A window that changes a few cells at every frame, a clock or a ticker, saves about a millisecond at every frame.

**The decisions**, each the scoping's recommendation.
1. **The repaint is the full paint under a clip, by one painter.**
   - The dirty rectangles are each named cell's rectangle, in each quadrant it lies in, widened along its row, before the patch and after, to the span its text spills over and to the span of any text from its left that spills into or through it.
   - Under a clip of their union, the viewport runs the full paint's own steps over the rows and columns they meet, in the full paint's order: the background, the fills, the gridlines, the texts, the selection and the marks, and the frozen separators. The headers are never repainted.

   *Alternative:* a painter of one cell, a second implementation of the paint, which would have to agree with the first on every rule above.

   (*Corrected 2026-10-15*, the build, where the tree and the rasterizer decided:
   - Each rectangle is painted under its own clip, over its own row's columns, not the union under one clip. Run once a rectangle under the union's clip, the steps would lay the selection's and the marks' translucent fills once a rectangle over every other; run once over the rows and columns the rectangles meet, they would visit every cell between two rectangles far apart. A row's rectangles are merged where they touch, so that no two overlap.
   - The text on a cell's left is looked for as far as the full paint looks, the quadrant's columns in view and eight before them, not eight from the cell. Every cell between that text and the cell is empty, so the nearest cell that holds anything is the one text that can spill into it, and on a wide view it may stand twelve columns away.
   - Where a cell's paint lies is found by the full paint's own code: the cell's paint run through a tracer, a painter that keeps the ops it would draw and draws nothing.
   - The full paint's own lines move. Each line in an opaque color is filled as a rectangle a device pixel wide, where all were stroked as one path. Chrome's CPU rasterizer strokes a long line a few pixels short of covered, and differently under another clip, so a repaint's few lines did not paint the full paint's pixels: a fuzz of random patches found 1 or 2 such pixels in 3 of its first 10, each the full paint's own, a gridline's pixel at about three quarters of its color. Filled, every line is exact on both rasterizers: on the GPU the fill paints the stroke's pixels exactly, 0 differing of 8.1 million at the owner's size, and on the CPU it removes the stroke's 273 short pixels there. A line in a color with alpha is stroked as before, so that a crossing blends once.)
2. **When it paints whole instead:**
   - before a full paint of the model since its load or its show;
   - when the scroller is not where the last paint left it, a scroll's event pending, or the canvas's size or ratio is not the last paint's;
   - when the cells named are more than a share of the cells in view, the crossover measured in the build, with a quarter as the prior.

   (*Measured 2026-10-15*, the build, headless Chrome 155 on the GPU at the owner's full screen, a sheet of 2,800 cells in view, one patch an animation frame, its time on the main thread: a repaint costs about 10.5 µs a cell for cells scattered one a row and about 6.8 for cells in runs of a row; a full paint of the dense sheet costs 6.9 to 7.7 ms. Scattered cells cross it near a fifth of the cells in view, between 512 and 640 cells; runs cross near two fifths. The prior, a quarter, stands between them, and is the share. A patch of one cell costs 0.10 to 0.14 ms the first time in a frame against 0.014 back to back, its model's work alone 0.032 against 0.005: a frame's cold start, not the paint.)
3. **The draw list describes the canvas.** After a repaint, `draws()` gives the last full paint's ops with each repainted cell's fill and text ops replaced by the repaint's, so every held window of the loop oracle stands as it is. The viewport counts its repaints.

   (*Corrected 2026-10-15*, the build: the list is laid over, not spliced at each repaint. The full paint notes where each quadrant's fills, gridlines, texts and ranges begin in its list. A repaint keeps, by quadrant, the fills and texts it drew for each cell whose paint it decided as the full paint does: the rectangle's own columns, drawn or not; a text it drew to their left; and, left of the columns in view, where the full paint looks back by the same rule, a text it did not draw too. `draws()` merges them into the full paint's sections in its order, by row, column and line, when an oracle asks, so a repaint builds no list.)
4. **The oracle: pixels.**
   - After every patched frame of the loop oracle's `changes` case, over the module, the canvas's pixels (`getImageData`) are held byte for byte to a full paint's of the same model and state, and the draw list op for op to a full paint's.
   - The case's card gains cells a repaint must get right: a number turning to #s; a long text spilling over empty neighbors, growing, shrinking, and cut by a neighbor that fills; a neighbor's spill restored when its blocker empties; a wrapped text; a look's fill turning on and off; a cell under the selection and one under a mark; a cell in each frozen quadrant; a cell in a hidden row; and a cell scrolled out of view, which repaints nothing.
   - The mutants, lettered after `ENGINE.19`'s, each failing by name: a repaint without the spill's widening; one without the left neighbor's; one with no clip; one that leaves out the selection; and one whose draw list keeps the old ops.
   - *The catch:* the build first probes whether Chrome's GPU canvas paints a clipped repaint to exactly a full paint's pixels. Where it does not, the oracle's viewport paints into a context made `willReadFrequently`, which Chrome rasterizes on the CPU.

   (*Corrected 2026-10-15*, the build, where the probe and the card decided:
   - *The catch, answered.* Chrome 155's GPU canvas paints a clipped repaint to exactly a full paint's pixels: 0 bytes differ over a crafted record, with and without frozen panes, under row bands and under cells' rectangles, each canvas read back once. But Chrome moves a canvas read back often to the CPU midway, and the CPU rasterizes text otherwise than the GPU, by up to 12 levels in 15,495 bytes of one full paint, so a repaint after five readbacks differed by 8,335. The oracle's viewports therefore paint on the CPU from the first: a viewport option, `willReadFrequently`, and, since the host makes its own viewport, a host option, `viewport`, passed to it, two lines of `web/host.js` the scoping's work did not name. Under `--disable-gpu`, as the check runs Chrome, both are the CPU's.
   - *The full paint compared with is a twin's,* a second viewport beside the host's that loads `host.record` and takes the view's frozen panes, selection and scroll, each a full paint. The oracle never paints the host's viewport whole, so its repaints pile up as they do in play.
   - *The card.* The fill moved from `A3:H10` to `C3:J10`, its 64 cells kept, to make room in the columns the view freezes for `A5` and a wrapped `B7`, and `J4`'s label went with it. `B7`'s texts wrap in two lines and in three, every line inside its row, since the window's hold joins the lines drawn and holds them to the record's text.
   - *The view's acts.* A selection over `K1:M2` and a mark over `L6:O6`, both translucent, from frame 0. Panes frozen two by two from 25 to 35, where the twin holds the window, since the oracle's own layout has no frozen panes: `drawnHeld` falls from 60 to 49, re-pinned with that reason. And the whole window scrolled out of view from 44 to 48, so that a cell out of view repainting nothing is held as a patch repainted with no rectangle, the canvas as the frame before left it.
   - *The crafted patches* are held the same way, and a patch of all 64 cells of a window of 8 by 8, more than a quarter of the cells in view, is painted whole (`crafted` 6 to 7).
   - *The mutants.* `BX` and `BZ` fail at the first crafted patch, with or without the module, so thirty-eight of the control's pages apply without it.)

## `ENGINE.7` — edit and continue: a rebuilt source applied to the running game, its state kept

*Scoped 2026-10-15 at the owner's word, who chose it that day as the roadmap's item that most helps every cartridge's authoring, Buffet's above all: today a rule changed is built and loaded, the game begins again at frame 0, and the state under test is reached again by hand. Its blocker, Frazaro's `KERNEL.34` (`d352774`, 2026-10-12), made a formula written into a running grid cost the time its cells take. The owner approved the fifteen decisions on 2026-10-16: "Recommendations approved; proceed with implementing ENGINE.7 as scoped." Read on the day: `web/host.js` (the load, the edit, the recorder, the player), the player's drawer in `web/index.template.html` (Build and Load), `engine/src/abi.rs` (`alonzo_expand`), `engine/src/cartridge.rs` (the manifest, the device layouts, the load's checks and the write's), and the write of `vla-lang` 0.9.4 in Frazaro's tree at its tag.*

**The item's text against the tree.** Each correction is also a dated note on the roadmap's line.
- *"The new cartridge's rows compared with those of the cartridge the host loaded."* After a first continue the grid holds the rebuilt cartridge's rules, so the next continue is compared with the cartridge the grid was last given, the one loaded or the one last applied (decision 10). The replay's header still names the cartridge loaded (decision 9).
- *"What a write cannot carry, a sheet added or removed, a line of the manifest, a device's layout."* The write takes `cell`, `formula` and `derived` rows and nothing else (`Machine::write_row`), and a `cell` row's value is a number, a text, a truth value or an error, so no write empties a cell (`load::datum`). So two more things are named and Load offered: every row that is not a cell or formula row (a column, a row's height, a format, a style, a look, a name), and a cell a removed row wrote that no row of the rebuilt cartridge writes (decisions 4 and 5). A device's layout is the page's, by the manifest's version and screen and by the sheets the grid holds (`Device::layout`), so it never changes apart from those.
- *"The next frame computed whole, as a formula's write makes it."* Measured below: after a formula row, whole, Sand's 189,215 cells in 24 ms, even after a formula of one cell; after value rows alone, the cells they reach, Sand's color in 0.6 ms.
- *The hand test's "the day and the cash are kept"* (the session's prompt). Buffet holds no cash yet, its Portfolio being a later dish. The state a continue keeps there is the frame, of which the day is a function (`Day!B3`), the market's die (`Dice!B1`, through its twin) and the four waves' phases (`Market!E8:E11`, taken on day 0 and held).

**Substrate, verified.**
- *The load* (`loadBytes`) stops the loop, unloads, resets the host's state, loads into a fresh handle, describes, writes a host seed, starts the replay's record from frame 0 and draws frame 0. `play` reloads `cartBytes`, the bytes loaded, so a replay plays on the file it names.
- *The edit* (`edit`) takes one `cell` or `formula` row, refused while a replay plays; it waits in `edits` and is written at the next frame's start as its own write, after the derived writes and the Input rows (`_issueInputs`, `_issueEdit`); at rate zero each edit is a frame. A landed edit is recorded as its row (`_recordEdit`), and an edit of the Input sheet makes the next frame's Input rows whole for the recorder and the host alike.
- *The recorder* writes a frame's rows as one form, `(frame n row ...)`, under a header naming the cartridge loaded by its SHA-256 and its seed; the player issues a frame's rows as one write after the derived writes, and refuses a frame holding any row but a cell or a formula.
- *Build* (`buildCartridge`) runs `host.expand` over the source's box, the path the command line uses and every library the page holds, puts the cartridge in its box and opens it, and loads nothing. *Load*, in the bar since `ENGINE.14`, loads the box from frame 0 and starts the loop.
- *The load's checks and the write's* (`Cartridge::load`, `Cartridge::write`). Both run the device layouts, the host cells and the Screen's size, and the machine refuses a cycle at both. The load alone refuses a cell written twice, a volatile function (`cart-formula-volatile`) and a plane's Palette out of order (`check_palette`). The machine's write applies its rows in order and undoes them all at a refusal; a formula that would read the same is not written; a write of a value or a formula into a running grid needs no new call.
- *The handles.* The language keeps 16 live (`HANDLES`), so a second handle beside the running one is free to take and give back.

**The measurements** (*measurement*, 2026-10-15, headless Chrome 155 at the owner's full screen, its processes pinned to the performance cores and opted out of power throttling, a fixed loop timed before and after each run: 326 and 324 ms over Buffet, 329 and 329 over Sand). A probe evaluated in a copy of each built page, Buffet's own page at `alonzo` 0.1.4 and Alonzo's at `a048b90`. For each edit it built the source by the page's pass, read both cartridges with the viewport's reader, compared their rows by sheet and address, and loaded the rebuilt cartridge in a second handle of the same module. For the costs it timed today's route, Build, Load and the committed replay played to the frame the continue reaches, on a fresh module. Then on another it played the cartridge to frame 1,800 (Buffet, a minute) or 2,085 (Sand, the owner's painting session), ran five frames, and applied the edit: the pass, the comparison, the second load and its unload, the write of the rows that differ between two frames, the frame after, and five frames more. Scratch only.
